payload.friendly_name: One landing proof for lane cleanup
payload.purpose_context: After a clean squash landing of a lanes_with_coord Mission, cleanup keeps every lane because the lanes carry older copies of tool-written Mission files, and doctor workspaces --prune refuses the same lanes. One shared landing proof sets those files aside only when the lane never authored them, and lanes with no usable proof are kept instead of going through the older remover (#7747, #7325).
payload.purpose_tldr: Consolidate and doctor remove every lane whose work has landed, and keep, with a named code, every lane they cannot prove landed.

payload.question: Which tool-written Mission files may the landing proof set aside, and on what evidence?
Which cleanup paths must share the landing proof?
What happens to a lane that reaches cleanup with no usable landing proof (no proof, no worktree, no branch, or an empty PASS tip)?
Which worktrees does doctor workspaces apply the set-aside to?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-22 (Ancestor blob + keep-code, relayed by the dispatcher, ledger R68): status.events.jsonl keeps its line-containment check; status.json, meta.json and tasks/WP*.md of the lane's own Mission are set aside only when the lane's blob is an ancestor version of the target's copy (the lane never authored it). Never trust a merge-tree or merge-driver result on kitty-specs/**. Everything else fails closed.
Operator ruling 2026-11-22: one public predicate in lanes/lane_tip.py used by both consolidate lane cleanup and doctor workspaces prune.
Operator ruling 2026-11-22: the lane is kept with a new named code (LANDING_PROOF_UNAVAILABLE); no change to the destructive guard.
Operator ruling 2026-11-22: only released Mission lanes (doctor gets the slug from the Mission meta for the lane); other worktrees keep the plain proof.

payload.question: After a squash landing the coordination history is gone from the target. How is 'the lane never authored it' proven: (A) from the lane's own commit graph, or (B) from the target plus a recorded coordination tip?

payload.rationale: Escalated to the operator via the dispatcher 2026-11-22 with repro evidence; awaiting ruling.

payload.final_answer: A: lane graph. Operator ruling 2026-11-23 (dispatcher ledger R71): a Mission bookkeeping file (status.json, meta.json, tasks/WP*.md of the lane's own Mission) is set aside only when both lane and target have it and no lane-own first-parent commit changed it, except a merge whose result equals its non-first parent's version; any merge-driver or conflict result counts as authored. status.events.jsonl keeps line containment; membership in the target's history still passes. One predicate for consolidate and doctor; everything else fails closed. The residual (a version merged in from a non-coordination branch) is recorded in the ADR 2026-11-06-1 amendment.

payload.question: With retain_branches (worktree removed, branch retained), does the worktree-only leg stay on today's guarded worktree removal, or is the lane kept with LANDING_PROOF_UNAVAILABLE?

payload.final_answer: Stay on guarded worktree removal (runner design, accepted by the dispatcher 2026-11-23; put to the operator, flips to keep-with-code if they rule otherwise). The leg deletes no branch, so it is not the #7325 blind spot, and the FR-033 retention report is unchanged.

payload.wp_title: No lane leaves through the older remover without a proof
The landing proof and consolidate adoption

payload.question: Operator confirmation of PD-1 (Decision Moment 01M84SX5): does the retained-branch leg stay on today's guarded worktree removal?

payload.final_answer: Yes, PD-1 stands. Decided by the operator 2026-11-23 (ruling 4A, relayed by the dispatcher); supersedes the runner's provisional resolution of 01M84SX5 as the record of who decided.
